(1) the proposed method outperforms all other algorithms in the first IV² database evaluation campaign; (2) the proposed method is very robust to illumination, expression, pose and image quality variability; (3) the proposed method can be used for face recognition in a wide variety of applications.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the performance of a 2D face identification algorithm on a database of real images, in the presence of variability.
the study of local features for 2D recognition and their selection.
the development of a new algorithm for 2D facial recognition based on local features extraction using SP, a feature selection by Adaboost and a non-linear classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method outperforms the state of the art in 2D face verification on IV² database.
the proposed method has shown its efficiency in terms of accuracy and speed, and that the combination of SP and Adaboost is a promising way for 2D facial recognition.

the algorithm presented in this paper is a very competitive approach for the 2D face identification problem, and it can be used in many applications where the quality of the images is not a constraint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is a robust one, able to recognize faces with high accuracy and with high speed.
the proposed algorithm outperforms the other algorithms in the case of illumination variability and is the best one when considering the whole variability.
the proposed method is robust to illumination, expression and pose changes, and it is also robust to quality variations of images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a good feature extraction and a good feature selection are the key points to achieve good performances in 2D face verification.
a good compromise can be found between the use of local features and the use of global ones, which can be a good alternative to global methods for 2D facial recognition.
a simple and fast algorithm, based on a non-linear classification method, can outperform more sophisticated methods, based on more complex feature extraction methods.
